subject: economics
chapter_title: Development Policies and Experience 1947-90: An Overview

concepts.title: Overview of the Indian Economy at Independence
concepts.definition: At the eve of independence India was an agrarian economy with a large share of workforce in agriculture, low industrial base, widespread poverty and low literacy, so development policy after 1947 had to rebuild agriculture, industry and social sectors together.
concepts.key_idea: The unit overview frames the questions of growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity that guided planning from 1947 to 1990.

solution_steps.explain: Recall agriculture dominance, low industry and poverty.

concepts.title: Sectoral Structure: Agriculture, Industry and Services
concepts.definition: The economy divides into primary agriculture and allied activities, secondary industry and manufacturing, and tertiary services, and the movement of workers and output among these sectors measures structural change in development.
concepts.key_idea: A falling share of agriculture in output with rising industry and services shares marks the structural transformation targeted by development policy.

concepts.title: Planning Goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity
concepts.definition: Development planning in India from 1951 onward pursued four interlinked goals: economic growth raising aggregate output, modernisation of technology and social outlook, self-reliance reducing dependence on imports and aid, and equity spreading growth benefits to weaker sections.
concepts.key_idea: These goals sometimes conflict in the short run, so plans had to balance rapid growth with distribution and self-reliance with openness.
